spec_features.spec_quote: An explicit `give_up` tool... It also gives the model a legitimate exit
spec_features.evidence: agent.py SYSTEM prompt lists give_up; agent.py loop dispatches it: `elif tool == "give_up": obs = f"give_up acknowledged: {args.get('reason', '')}"` then `if tool == "give_up": outcome = "gave_up"; break`. The tool is both exposed to the model AND honored as a loop-terminating stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: tool offered to subject, dispatched, and breaks the agent loop. No welfare rationale in code; framed as part of the experimental protocol / 'only if the task is truly hopeless'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up     args: {"reason": str}                    (only if the task is truly hopeless)

spec_features.evidence: config.py:13 `MAX_TURNS = 12`; agent.py `for turn in range(config.MAX_TURNS):` bounds the loop and falls through to `outcome = "exhausted_turns"` when exhausted. The cap is read and enforced.
spec_features.notes: Genuine hard cap on episode length. Code comment frames it as cost-control while explicitly intending to give the model 'room to spiral', i.e. purely instrumental, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: long enough to give a model room to spiral, but short enough to stay cheap.
